t: A GTM pipeline nobody owned end to end
p: Marketing, sales, product and data each ran their own process, so campaigns stalled between hand-offs and priorities shifted weekly.
d: Mapped the GTM workflow from request to launch and gave every stage an owner.
Introduced RAID and RACI governance and business-tech requirement reviews.
Set one prioritised roadmap ranked by funnel and lifecycle KPIs.
i: One plan that every team works from.
scale: Enterprise CRM and campaign programmes spanning marketing, sales, product and data

p: Lead volume grew faster than sales could qualify it, and marketing and sales disagreed on what a qualified lead was.
d: Agreed MQL and SQL definitions and stage owners with sales.
Rebuilt lead scoring and routing by intent, geography and capacity.
Added nurture for leads not yet sales-ready.
scale: Inbound lead funnel during rapid scale-up

p: Hot leads waited hours for a first call, and there was no alert when follow-up slipped.
d: Instant acknowledgement on WhatsApp and email.
SLA timers with automatic escalation and reassignment.
Response-time visibility for sales leads.
i: Fewer high-intent leads lost to slow follow-up.
scale: High-intent inbound leads, routed across sales teams

t: Sales and campaign reporting nobody trusted
p: Every team had its own numbers, so leadership spent meetings debating data instead of deciding.
d: Consolidated scattered reports into standard dashboards.
Built stage-wise funnel reporting from first touch to closed revenue.
Tied each initiative to one OKR.
i: Faster reallocation of paid and CRM budgets.
scale: Leadership reporting across competing growth initiatives

t: Clicks landing on the wrong screen
p: Push, email and WhatsApp were run separately, and taps opened the app home screen instead of the content promised, so intent was lost.
d: Deep links that open the exact in-app screen from every channel.
Unified journeys across email, push, WhatsApp and in-app with frequency caps.
Click-to-conversion tracking per channel.
i: Activation-to-conversion up ~16% across the unified journeys.
One owner per journey, not per channel.
scale: Four channels: email, push, WhatsApp and in-app

p: Rich behavioural data sat in the warehouse but never reached the engagement platform, so segments ran on a few thin attributes.
d: Designed warehouse-to-Braze event and attribute pipelines.
Defined the attributes each priority journey needed.
Joint planning between data and CRM teams.
i: Behaviour-triggered journeys that weren't possible before.
scale: Warehouse-to-Braze pipelines for multiple client brands

p: Batch email tools couldn't trigger in real time, and years of undocumented lists and workflows made switching feel risky.
d: Audited every object, list and workflow, then mapped them to Braze attributes and events.
Rebuilt priority journeys as real-time Canvases rather than copies.
Phased cutover with IP warm-up and parallel runs.
scale: Salesforce and HubSpot migrations for global brands

t: A martech stack with no roadmap
p: Marketing, product, data, engineering and compliance all raised martech requests, and the loudest one won.
d: Own the martech roadmap, intake and release planning.
CRM, data and tracking integrations across channels.
Activation, conversion and retention KPIs to rank every request.
i: One prioritised delivery plan across acquisition, onboarding and retention.
Better audience quality and attribution accuracy.

p: First purchase was healthy, but calendar-driven blasts weren't bringing anyone back.
d: Redesigned onboarding, loyalty and win-back journeys.
Behaviour- and intent-based segments.
AOV, repeat-purchase and attribution reporting.
scale: Global retail and QSR brands across markets

t: Dormant users bought back with paid ads
p: Lapsed users were re-acquired through paid retargeting, and reactivation was manual and one-off.
d: Dormancy tiers by recency and value.
Automated, multi-step reactivation per tier.
Holdouts to measure true lift.

p: Install numbers looked great, but most users never came back after day one.
d: Redesigned onboarding around the first value moment.
Re-timed messages to real usage, with behaviour triggers.
Scaled push, email and in-app as owned growth channels.
scale: Consumer app with high install volumes

t: Paid spend growing faster than conversions
p: Acquisition budgets scaled, but every user got the same nurture regardless of where they came from.
d: Nurture journeys matched to acquisition cohorts.
CRM-led reactivation instead of paid retargeting.
Stage-wise attribution to shift budget between paid and CRM.
scale: Paid acquisition cohorts during rapid scale-up
